Two review findings against the legacy-install migration (packages/cli/src/lib/legacy-migration.ts).

1. `isGeneratedWrapper` decides whether a command wrapper is one we generated and may rewrite. Today it accepts any wrapper whose bundle path merely ends in the legacy file name, for any harness. It must only accept a wrapper that is byte-for-byte what we would have generated for this exact legacy bundle path and this wrapper's own harness. Change it to `isGeneratedWrapper(content, bundlePath, harness?)`, where `bundlePath` is the full path of the legacy bundle and `harness` is the harness the wrapper launches (omitted for the main command). A wrapper pointing at another bundle that shares the file name, or at the right bundle with a different harness, is not ours. Update the callers.

2. The check for whether the legacy login service is still loaded treats every nonzero result as "not loaded", including launchctl or systemctl failing to start, timing out or being killed. A failed check can therefore delete the service file of a service that is still running. Only a real exit code should count as an answer; anything else must keep the file so it is retried on the next start.

This is a pnpm monorepo. Run one test file with `cd packages/tests && node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/<file>.test.ts`; do not run the whole suite. packages/cli imports @nconnect/models from its build output, so after changing packages/models run `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p packages/models/tsconfig.json` from the repository root. Dependencies are already installed: never run pnpm, npm or any install command. Do not bump versions or edit CHANGELOG or the site/ folder.
